answer: Each action is accepted only with a threshold signature from agents holding scarce, stake-backed credentials issued through independent registrars; the beacon publishes the current validator set, while a zenith checkpoint records accepted attestations so identities cannot cheaply reset their history. A sybil attacker must acquire and lock real stake across enough registrars to control a quorum, then risks slashing for conflicting signatures. The canyon between creating names and gaining voting weight makes mass fake accounts expensive, though compromised credentials remain a risk.
